front: What is the default administrative distance of OSPF on Cisco IOS?
Which IP protocol number and multicast addresses does OSPFv2 use?
back: IP protocol 89. 224.0.0.5 reaches all OSPF routers; 224.0.0.6 reaches the DR and BDR.

front: What are the LSDB and SPF in OSPF?
back: The LSDB is the area map built from LSAs, identical on every router. SPF calculates each router's lowest-cost paths from it.

front: How do DBD and LSU packets differ?
back: A DBD lists the LSAs a router holds. An LSU carries the LSAs themselves.

front: In what order does IOS choose the OSPF router ID?
back: 1. The router-id command. 2. Highest IPv4 address on an up loopback. 3. Highest IPv4 address on any other up interface.

front: You change router-id on an OSPF process that already has neighbors. What makes the new RID take effect?
back: clear ip ospf process (or a reload). It drops that process's adjacencies while they form again.

front: Which can differ between two OSPF neighbors: the process ID or the area ID?
back: The process ID. It is local to each router. The area ID must match.

front: What are the default OSPF Hello and dead intervals on broadcast and point-to-point interfaces?
back: Hello 10 seconds, dead 40 seconds. The dead interval defaults to four times the Hello.

front: Which values must match before two OSPF routers become neighbors?
back: Area ID, subnet and mask, Hello and dead intervals, and authentication if configured. Their router IDs must be different.

front: What do the 2-Way and Full neighbor states mean?
back: 2-Way: each router has seen its own RID in the other's Hello. Full: the two link-state databases are synchronized.

front: A neighbor is stuck in ExStart or Exchange. What is the usual cause?
back: An MTU mismatch between the two interfaces. Make the MTUs equal.

front: When is a 2WAY/DROTHER neighbor state normal?
back: Between two DROTHERs on a broadcast segment. Each is Full only with the DR and BDR.

front: What decides a new DR election, and what breaks a tie?
back: The highest interface priority (default 1) wins. The highest router ID breaks a tie.

front: What does OSPF interface priority 0 do?
back: The router can never be DR or BDR on that segment. It still becomes Full with the DR and BDR.

front: A router with a higher priority joins a segment that already has a DR and BDR. What happens?
back: Nothing changes. The election is non-preemptive, so the new router is a DROTHER.

front: What happens on a broadcast segment when the DR fails?
back: The BDR becomes DR. A new BDR is elected from the remaining eligible routers.

front: How do the OSPF broadcast and point-to-point network types differ?
back: Broadcast elects a DR and BDR. Point-to-point elects neither, and the neighbor shows FULL/ -.

front: Which command makes an Ethernet link between two routers an OSPF point-to-point link?
back: ip ospf network point-to-point, on both interfaces.

front: How does IOS calculate an OSPF interface cost?
back: Reference bandwidth ÷ interface bandwidth, rounded down, minimum 1. The default reference is 100 Mbps.

front: What is the default OSPF cost of FastEthernet, GigabitEthernet and 10-Gigabit Ethernet interfaces?
back: 1 for all three, because the default reference bandwidth is only 100 Mbps.

front: Which command sets the OSPF reference bandwidth to 10 Gbps?
back: auto-cost reference-bandwidth 10000 in router configuration mode. The value is in Mbps; use it on every router.

front: Which wins: the calculated OSPF cost or ip ospf cost?
back: ip ospf cost. It overrides the bandwidth calculation on that interface.

front: Which interface costs add up to an OSPF route's metric?
back: The outgoing interface cost at each router along the path, including the last router's interface onto the destination network.

front: What does [110/11] mean in an OSPF route?
back: Administrative distance 110, OSPF cost 11.

front: What are the two ways to enable OSPFv2 on an interface?
back: network ADDRESS WILDCARD area AREA in router mode, or ip ospf PROCESS area AREA on the interface.

front: What is the wildcard mask for a /30, subnet mask 255.255.255.252?
back: 0.0.0.3. Subtract each octet of the subnet mask from 255.

front: An interface is 172.16.5.33/27. Which prefix does network 172.16.5.33 0.0.0.0 area 0 advertise?
back: 172.16.5.32/27. The wildcard only selects the interface; the interface's own mask sets the prefix.

front: What does a passive OSPF interface do?
back: It sends no Hellos, so no neighbor forms on it. Its network is still advertised through other interfaces.

front: Which command makes an OSPF router advertise a default route?
back: default-information originate in router mode. The router needs a default route of its own unless you add always.

front: Neighbors are Full but a remote LAN has no OSPF route. What do you check first?
back: That the LAN interface on the far router is up and enabled in OSPF.
